title: Problem words
intro: These thirty-six sets of words are the ones that cost Vietnamese writers the most marks, either because they sound the same, because one Vietnamese word covers both, or because English splits a meaning where Vietnamese does not. Each row gives the difference in one line and one example of each word, so you can check a doubt in a few seconds. Learn the example sentences rather than the definitions: it is the pattern around the word that tells you which one you need.

tables.caption: Words that sound the same, or nearly the same
rows: their · there · they're
*their* = belonging to them · *there* = in that place, or introducing existence · *they're* = they are
**Their** bus was late. · **There** are two routes to Huế. · **They're** waiting at the gate.
its · it's
*its* = belonging to it (no apostrophe) · *it's* = it is or it has
The city has lost **its** river view. · **It's** raining again.
your · you're
*your* = belonging to you · *you're* = you are
Bring **your** dictionary. · **You're** the first to finish.
affect · effect
*affect* is the verb; *effect* is the noun you have **an** effect **on** something
Noise **affects** concentration. · Noise has a clear **effect** on concentration.
then · than
*then* = next, or at that time · *than* = the word used in comparisons
We ate, **then** we walked home. · Đà Lạt is cooler **than** Cần Thơ.
to · too · two
*to* = direction or the infinitive · *too* = also, or more than enough · *two* = the number 2
I cycle **to** school. · The bag was **too** heavy. · I have **two** brothers.
loose · lose
*loose* is an adjective meaning not tight · *lose* is a verb meaning stop having
The chain is **loose**. · Don't **lose** your ticket.
accept · except
*accept* = say yes to something · *except* = apart from
She **accepted** the offer. · Everyone came **except** Long.
advice · advise
*advice* is the uncountable noun · *advise* is the verb
She gave me good **advice**. · She **advised** me to apply early.
practice · practise
In British spelling, *practice* is the noun and *practise* is the verb
We need more **practice**. · We **practise** every Thursday.
principal · principle
*principal* = main, or the head of a college · *principle* = a rule or a belief
The **principal** reason is cost. · She refused on **principle**.
complement · compliment
*complement* = complete or go well with · *compliment* = say something nice
The sauce **complements** the fish. · He paid her a **compliment**.
stationary · stationery
*stationary* = not moving · *stationery* = paper, pens and envelopes
The bus was **stationary** for ten minutes. · She bought **stationery** for the new term.

tables.caption: Verbs that are easy to swap
rows: rise · raise
*raise* takes an object; *rise* never does
Prices **rise** every summer. · The shop **raised** its prices in June.
lie · lay
*lie – lay – lain* = rest, no object · *lay – laid – laid* = put something down
She **lay** on the sofa for an hour. · He **laid** the books on the desk.
lose · miss
You *lose* an object you owned; you *miss* a bus, a class or a chance
I **lost** my umbrella. · I **missed** the last bus.
borrow · lend
*borrow* = take from someone · *lend* = give to someone for a while
Can I **borrow** your charger? · She **lent** me her charger.
bring · take
*bring* is towards the speaker; *take* is away from the speaker
**Bring** your notes to my office. · **Take** these forms to the office.
say · tell
*say* something; *tell* someone something
She **said** that the test was easy. · She **told** us that the test was easy.
hear · listen to
*hear* just happens; *listen to* is something you choose to do
I **heard** a noise outside. · I **listen to** podcasts on the bus.
remember · remind
*remember* = keep in your mind · *remind* = make someone else remember
I **remembered** her birthday. · Please **remind** me about the deadline.
used to · be used to
*used to* + base verb = a past habit · *be used to* + -ing = be accustomed to
I **used to** cycle to school. · I **am used to** cycling in the rain.

tables.caption: Nouns, adjectives and quantity words
rows: economic · economical
*economic* = about the economy · *economical* = saving money
**Economic** growth slowed in 2023. · A scooter is an **economical** way to travel.
effective · efficient
*effective* = it produces the result you wanted · *efficient* = it uses little time, money or energy
The campaign was **effective**: smoking fell. · The new engine is more **efficient**.
historic · historical
*historic* = important in history · *historical* = relating to the past
A **historic** decision for the region. · A **historical** novel set in 1945.
sensible · sensitive
*sensible* = showing good judgement · *sensitive* = easily affected or easily hurt
That was a **sensible** choice. · She is **sensitive** to criticism.
interested · interesting
*-ed* is how a person feels; *-ing* is what causes the feeling
I am **interested** in history. · The lecture was **interesting**.
fewer · less
*fewer* + plural count nouns · *less* + uncountable nouns
**Fewer** students take the bus now. · There is **less** traffic at the weekend.
amount · number
*a number of* + count nouns · *an amount of* + uncountable nouns
A large **number** of applicants. · A large **amount** of rainfall.
much · many
*many* + plural count nouns · *much* + uncountable nouns
**Many** problems remain. · **Much** research has been done.
between · among
*between* = two things, or several things seen separately · *among* = inside a larger group
The gap **between** the two figures. · Popular **among** first-year students.
beside · besides
*beside* = next to · *besides* = in addition to
She sat **beside** the window. · **Besides** English, he speaks Japanese.
job · work
*job* is a count noun; *work* is uncountable
She has a part-time **job**. · She has a lot of **work** this week.
trip · journey · travel
*trip* = the whole short visit · *journey* = the act of going from A to B · *travel* is normally the verb
A three-day **trip** to Sa Pa. · The **journey** takes six hours. · They **travel** by train.
in time · on time
*in time* = early enough for something · *on time* = at exactly the right time
We arrived **in time** to buy tickets. · The train left **on time**.
specially · especially
*specially* = for one particular purpose · *especially* = above all, more than the others
The room was **specially** prepared for the exam. · The summer is hot, **especially** in June.

notes: The apostrophe test settles four of these rows at once: if you can say *it is*, *they are* or *you are* in the sentence, write *it's*, *they're* or *you're*. If you cannot, write *its*, *their* or *your*.
*rise* and *raise* follow the same test as many other pairs: look for an object. If a noun follows the verb, you need the verb that takes one — *raise prices*, *lay the table*, *lend me a pen*.
*advice* and *practice* are the nouns; the -se spellings are verbs. A quick check in British English: if you can put *some* or *a piece of* in front, you want *advice*.

Some pairs exist in English because one Vietnamese word covers both. *tăng* covers *rise* and *raise*; *nhiều* covers *much* and *many*; *kinh tế* covers *economic* and *economical*; *lỡ* and *mất* are both often translated as *lose*. Whenever you translate one of these words, stop and check the row.
